questions.text: Why does CSRF rely on browser behavior?

answers.text: Because browsers automatically include cookies and credentials for same-origin requests
Because browsers block all cross-site requests
Because servers always ask for user confirmation

questions.text: An attacker builds a page that submits a hidden form to transfer money on your banking site. What is the best immediate defense?

answers.text: Validate an anti-CSRF token on the transfer endpoint

questions.text: Setting cookies to `SameSite=Strict` can reduce CSRF risk.
Name one additional header you can check server-side to help detect cross-site requests.
Which SameSite cookie value will still allow typical navigation from external sites but protects some CSRF cases?
True or False: Relying only on client-side JavaScript checks is a safe way to prevent CSRF.
Which action should require an extra confirmation even if the request looks valid?

answers.text: Money transfers or changing email address

questions.text: Level 2: When checking `Origin`/`Referer` headers for CSRF defense, what should you be mindful of?

answers.text: Some browsers or requests may omit these headers, so use as part of a layered defense
They are always present and fully reliable
